reasons: The tests are written to fail on throws, missing claims and swapped columns.
The file comments describe earlier mutation checks, which are not reproduced here.
I did not run these tests in this review.

terms.meaning: the page content produced as text without a browser
a fixed reference case used to test the system
a deliberate small change to code to check that a test catches it
a test pattern that runs the same check once for each item in a list

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and the reason it exists
sections.what: Brings in the views, components, helper functions and generated data, and explains that this file is the one that actually draws the views.
sections.why: The header says the build compiles the code without running it, so a separate check is needed.
sections.watch_out: The imports must match the real file names.

sections.name: text
sections.title: Plain text from a page
sections.what: Removes the tags from drawn HTML so the tests can search the readable words.
sections.why: The header says this is deliberately crude, so that a bug in a converter does not appear as a bug in the view.
sections.watch_out: Text is joined with spaces, so a phrase split across tags may not match.

sections.name: every view renders against the collected artefacts
sections.title: Each view draws and shows its stamp
sections.what: Checks that there are exactly three views with the expected names, and that each one draws a page with the depth tier shown and a substantial amount of content.
sections.why: The header says the prose describes three views, and a fourth would make that prose wrong without anyone noticing.
sections.watch_out: The count check must change whenever a view is added or removed.

sections.name: every golden case renders on the process view
sections.title: Each case draws on the process view
sections.what: For every golden case, checks that the client name appears and that the note saying five is worse on the inverted scores appears.
sections.why: The header says the scores are the section most likely to drop out silently.
sections.watch_out: The test depends on the golden cases in the data.

sections.name: the run stamp carries the standard of evidence on every view
sections.title: Stamp on every view
sections.what: Checks that each view shows the depth tier and every model name from the manifest.
sections.why: The header says a reader of any printed page must know what produced it.
sections.watch_out: The models come from the manifest. A new model is only checked if it is listed there.

sections.name: an absent record is a finding, not an empty page
sections.title: Missing record shows a finding
sections.what: Draws a case that was never collected and checks that the page names the missing file and shows no figures.
sections.why: An earlier version of this check searched the source code for phrases, so it would still pass if the branch were deleted.
sections.watch_out: The test checks that words such as FTE do not appear. A legitimate label containing those words would make it fail.

sections.name: the confidence derivation is honest at the layer a reader sees (part 1)
sections.title: Confidence view shows its working
sections.what: Checks that each case says agreement was not measured and shows the formula pieces. Also checks that a measured record shows as measured, with the agreement factor in the formula.
sections.why: The comments say a review once restored a broken label and the tests still passed, so this checks the wording a reader actually sees.
sections.watch_out: The exact wording is checked, so any rewording needs the test to change too.

sections.name: the confidence derivation is honest at the layer a reader sees (part 2)
sections.title: Inconsistent record is flagged on the page
sections.what: Draws a record with an agreement value but no matching declaration, and checks that the page shows the invalid record message.
sections.why: The viewer reads files that may not have been checked by the schema, so the page must say so.
sections.watch_out: The test checks part of the message text only.

sections.name: the band-comparability disclosure reaches the page (part 1)
sections.title: Band notice on every view
sections.what: Checks that the notice about bands not being comparable across the schema change appears on every view, next to the schema version, and is not hidden by an attribute.
sections.why: The notice has to be seen where it is used. Text inside a hidden element still counts as text, so the test checks the hiding attributes too.
sections.watch_out: This checks attributes only. The style rules that hide or show the notice are covered elsewhere.

sections.name: the band-comparability disclosure reaches the page (part 2)
sections.title: Band table rows checked one by one
sections.what: Confirms the table has one row per record, that narrowed rows are the ones with cited value parameters, that held rows are not, and that each figure sits in its own column.
sections.why: An earlier test searched the whole page, so swapping two columns still passed while the table showed the opposite of the disclosure.
sections.watch_out: Column positions are fixed numbers in this test, so adding a column means updating every index.

sections.name: the band-comparability disclosure reaches the page (part 3)
sections.title: Engine disagreement checks
sections.what: Checks that the viewer reports drift when its recalculated widening factor differs from the engine's, and that it agrees with the engine on every golden process.
sections.why: The viewer recalculates the factor on purpose so it can catch drift in the engine.
sections.watch_out: The drift amount used in the test is a chosen value, not one taken from the engine.

sections.name: the narrowing claim withdraws itself when the pattern breaks
sections.title: Narrowing claim withdraws when the pattern breaks
sections.what: Checks that the claim comes back false when an unevidenced process narrows, or an evidenced one does not. Also checks that the page drops its claim when the data breaks the pattern.
sections.why: The comments say a condition that is never reached in tests is only decoration, so both branches must run.
sections.watch_out: The changed data is a copy of the artifacts. The test relies on the page reading that copy.

summary: A test file that draws every view and checks that the key figures and disclosures appear on the rendered page.
purpose: Catches a view that crashes on real data, and checks that required warnings and notices reach the reader.
why: The header says the earlier test suite only checked helper functions, so a view could crash on every render while every test passed. This file was written to close that gap.
how: Renders each view, and each golden case on the process view, into plain text. Then searches that text for required phrases, checks the rows of the band table one by one, and checks that conditional claims disappear when the data breaks the pattern.
inputs: The generated artifacts file, the app, the components, the portfolio view and helper functions.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: Matching plain text is crude, so a rewording breaks a test. The tests check attributes and some style text, not the real browser appearance. The comments report counts from an earlier review, which I did not reproduce.
debug: If a test throws, draw that view directly and read the error. If a phrase is missing, search the view for the phrase. If band table tests fail, check the row and column order.
